novel_features.name: Digest
novel_features.description: Turns a lot's upcoming schedule into ready-to-paste announcement text instead of raw structured data.
novel_features.rationale: Office coordinators currently hand-copy truck names and times from the website into Slack every week; this produces that exact text block in one command.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when the task is 'summarize this week's schedule for humans,' not 'give me structured data.'

novel_features.name: Cuisine Alert
novel_features.description: Finds every upcoming shift at a lot matching a cuisine, without opening each shift page one at a time.
novel_features.rationale: The API only exposes cuisine tags nested one shift at a time under that shift's menu; no query filters the schedule by cuisine directly.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this when a user names a cuisine and a lot rather than a specific date — it walks the whole visible schedule window for you.

novel_features.name: Truck Schedule
novel_features.description: Shows every lot a specific truck visits, past and future — a view the Best Food Trucks website itself never built.
novel_features.rationale: bestfoodtrucks.com is entirely lot-centric; there is no page anywhere on the site that lists everywhere a given truck goes.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this to answer 'when does my favorite truck come back' or 'what other lots does this truck serve' — impossible from the live site's own navigation.
novel_features.group: Truck-centric views the website never built

novel_features.name: Market Hotlist
novel_features.description: Ranks trucks operating in a city by review signal, a cross-truck aggregate the site never computes.
novel_features.rationale: Rating data is scoped per shift/order in the API; nothing on the live site ranks trucks against each other within a market.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this for 'what's the best-rated truck in this city' rather than checking trucks one at a time.
novel_features.group: Truck-centric views the website never built

novel_features.name: Route Planner
novel_features.description: Combines multiple lots' schedules into one view in a single command instead of visiting each lot's page separately.
novel_features.rationale: The website requires navigating to each lot's URL individually; there is no multi-lot combined schedule view.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this when a user tracks more than one regular lot (e.g., office campus plus a nearby favorite) and wants one combined answer.

narrative.headline: The only Best Food Trucks client that can tell you where a truck goes, not just what's parked outside today.
narrative.value_prop: Best Food Trucks has no public API, no SDK, and no way to ask 'where else does this truck park' or 'summarize this week for my team.' This CLI talks directly to the same GraphQL backend the website and mobile apps use, then adds schedule digests, cuisine search, truck-centric reverse lookup, and cross-lot views the live site was never built to answer.

quickstart.comment: Confirms the CLI can reach the API. No login or API key needed — the read surface is fully anonymous.
See the full upcoming schedule for a specific lot by its URL slug.
Get the same schedule as ready-to-paste announcement text.
Look up a specific scheduled truck visit's full menu, prices, and hours.
Reverse-lookup: see every lot a specific truck visits, a view the website itself never shows.

troubleshoots.symptom: lot get returns 'not found' for a slug you copied from a URL
troubleshoots.fix: Use market list <city> to find the correct seoName slug — some lots have display names that differ from their URL slug.

troubleshoots.symptom: shift get returns an empty menu
troubleshoots.fix: The shift may not have started publishing its menu yet (workStatusHuman: 'Not Started'); menus typically populate closer to the shift's start time.
The market has zero trucks on record, or every truck lookup in the fan-out failed — check the fetch_failures field in --json output for per-truck error detail.

narrative.when_to_use: Use this CLI for anonymous, read-only lookups of Best Food Trucks lot schedules, truck rotations, and menu data — checking what's at a specific office campus or lot, tracking a favorite truck's schedule across lots, or summarizing a week's schedule for a team. It is the right tool whenever a task needs structured or human-readable schedule/menu data faster than clicking through the bot-protected website by hand.
anti_triggers: Do not use this CLI to place real food orders or complete checkout — order-ahead requires a customer login and payment method, which this CLI does not automate.
Do not use this CLI to manage a customer's 'subscribe to lot schedule' notification preferences — that also requires a logged-in customer session not exercised by this build.
Do not use this CLI as a general nationwide food-truck search engine beyond lots/trucks/markets already known to Best Food Trucks — it only knows what Best Food Trucks itself tracks.

recipes.title: What's at my office today
recipes.explanation: Pulls just today/tomorrow's truck name from the full schedule payload, instead of parsing the whole nested response by hand.

recipes.title: Paste this week's schedule into Slack
recipes.explanation: Produces the announcement text directly — no manual copy-paste from the website required.

recipes.title: Find every Thai truck coming to my lot
recipes.explanation: Walks the visible schedule window and filters by cuisine tag, something no single API call does server-side.

recipes.title: Track a favorite truck across every lot it visits
recipes.explanation: Reverse lookup with --select narrows a potentially large history-plus-future list down to just the two fields an agent needs to answer 'when and where.'

recipes.title: Combine two lots you care about into one view
recipes.explanation: One command instead of visiting two separate lot pages and manually merging the results.
